style: 1981 neon-noir chase cue in the Tangerine Dream / Thief school, analogue hardware only, dialogue shouted and talked over it, nobody sings. Sequencer bass racing in sixteenths at 150 BPM, a little ragged against the grid; huge gated-reverb snare cracking on two and four; icy minor-key polysynth pads underneath; the ambulance siren faked by two detuned oscillators sweeping up and down. Rain drumming the van roof, close mics, panic. Voices: a rough young woman with a smoker's rasp screaming the numbers; a man talking low, quick and clipped until his nerve snaps; a driver whose yell is thin, strained and cracking high. Red light: the sequencer locks onto one sustained bass pitch and a resonant low-pass sweeps it closed, drums gone. A plummy, petulant man whines down a tinny 1980s car telephone. Final beat: a pure flat oscillator tone, the score cut dead beneath it, then dead air.
exclude: singing, sung melody, chorus, rap, choir, upbeat, happy, funk, comedy, synthwave vocals, autotune, guitar solo, fade-out, music under the tone
lyrics:
[Intro: sixteenth-note sequencer bass, gated snare, oscillator siren]

[Spoken, female, rasping scream]
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!

[Spoken, male, low and clipped]
Sats dropping, he's peri-arrest!

[Spoken, male driver, cracking high yell]
Two minutes out! Get the fuck out of the way!

[Break: sequencer frozen to one bass pitch, filter closing, drums out]

[Spoken, male, nerve snapping]
Why have we stopped?!

[Spoken, posh man, tinny car telephone]
I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!

[Spoken, female, whisper]
Fifty over twen—

[Outro: flat oscillator tone alone]

[Silence]

[End]
title: PL r3-analog-synth-chase
